data.name: Fudayal
data.gender_notes: Fudayal is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'fadila', meaning 'to help, support, and assist'. In Islamic history, Fudayal refers to those who supported and aided the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) during the early days of Islam. The name Fudayal carries the meaning “Helper, Supporter” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Fudayal usually hope their child will grow to embody helper, supporter and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the importance of supporting and aiding others in their spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Fudayal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper, Supporter.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fudayal total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Fudayal holds a rich cultural significance in Islamic history as it refers to those individuals who stood by and aided the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) during the early days of Islam. The term Fudayis (plural of Fudayal) was used to describe the loyal companions of the Prophet, who pledged to support him and defend Islam against its enemies. These individuals were selfless, brave, and dedicated, and played a crucial role in the spread and preservation of the new faith.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Fudayal represents the importance of supporting and aiding one another in the path of righteousness. It is a reminder of the value of unity, commitment, and sacrifice in the service of Allah and His Messenger. The name inspires us to embody the qualities of Fudayis - being selfless, brave, and dedicated to the divine cause. Moreover, it emphasizes the role of each individual in contributing to the greater collective good of the Ummah (Muslim community).
